result: In 19 CDC-criteria CFS patients vs 17 controls, basal plasma MHPG was significantly lower and plasma 5-HIAA higher; CSF MHPG, 5-HIAA and HVA were measured but no CSF difference is reported.
reason: Finding is CSF DOPA/DOPAC/DHPG; the positive results here are plasma MHPG/5-HIAA, and the abstract reports no CSF result, so it does not test the claim and no other finding fits.

result: HMPAO SPECT in 60 CFS vs 14 controls showed lower cortical/cerebellar rCBF ratios across multiple regions (P<0.05), with 80% of patients having at least one reduced region (frontal 63%, parietal 53%).
reason: Independent resting SPECT cohort, same measure and direction; small control group, semi-quantitative ratios, no OI assessment.

result: In four Nevada-California CFS clusters followed 3 years, no link to EBV, HHV-6 or HTLV-I/II was found; giardiasis appeared to precipitate one cluster and nearly all cases returned to pre-illness activity.
reason: Only an anecdotal attribution of one cluster to giardiasis; no exposed-vs-unexposed rates or CFS prevalence after Giardia, so it does not measure what the Bergen finding claims.

result: After 3 years of follow-up almost all outbreak-cluster CFS cases had returned to pre-illness activity, and the authors judged prognosis usually favourable.
reason: Measures recovery and finds the opposite of rare recovery, so not a replication; weak because outbreak cases, a local case definition and no recovery numbers are given.

result: In 14 CFS patients vs 12 controls, all patients reported unrefreshing sleep and showed a prominent alpha EEG NREM sleep anomaly (p<=0.001) without physiological daytime sleepiness.
reason: Reports sleep microstructure (alpha intrusion), which the finding detail notes as a separate signal, not the latency/WASO/efficiency claim; adds rather than replicates.

result: EBV antibody titres did not differ between 14 CFS patients and 12 healthy controls.
reason: Same measure, same null direction, independent cohort; very small sample.

result: In 30 CFS patients vs 72 controls, evening plasma cortisol (89.0 vs 148.4 nmol/L, P<0.01) and 24-h urinary free cortisol (122.7 vs 203.1 nmol/24 h, P<0.0002) were lower, with raised evening ACTH.
reason: Independent cohort measuring 24-h urinary free cortisol and basal cortisol, lower in patients, same direction.

result: Graded ACTH dosing showed increased adrenocortical sensitivity but a reduced maximal cortisol response (P=0.0015), ACTH responses to oCRH were blunted (128.0 vs 225.4 pmol/L.min, P<0.04) and CSF CRH was normal, read as mild central adrenal insufficiency.
reason: Shows a blunted maximal cortisol response to ACTH but with increased sensitivity, blunted pituitary response to CRH and no glucocorticoid-suppression test, so it adds a central mechanism rather than plainly replicating enhanced feedback.

result: Flow cytometry in 147 CFS patients showed fewer CD8 suppressor cells and higher CD38 and HLA-DR on CD8 cells, significant (p=0.01) in patients with major symptoms and absent in 80 healthy, 22 contact and 43 disease controls, and unrelated to viral serology.
reason: Measures CD8 activation markers, not exhaustion transcription or chromatin; fits better the T-cell finding that activated lymphocytes go with more severe illness.

result: Serum bioactive TGF-beta was higher in CFS (290 vs 104 pg/mL, P<0.01), LPS-stimulated PBMC release of IL-1beta, IL-6 and TNF-alpha was higher (P<0.05), PHA-stimulated IL-6 was higher, and LPS-stimulated TGF-beta release was lower.
reason: Does not test blood handling; the stimulated PBMC hyperresponse matches innate hyperreactivity, and the serum TGF-beta rise is one of the elevations the meta-analysis pools, with the artefact caveat applying.
